The European Investment Bank Group’s international development arm, EIB Global, and First City Monument Bank have announced financing totalling €85m to support private-sector companies across agricultural value chains in Nigeria. At least 70 per cent of the financing will target cocoa and dairy value chains. The announcement was made during the Annual Meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank Group in Bangkok in the presence of EIB Group President Nadia Calviño, Nigerian Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy Taiwo Oyedele, EIB Vice-President Ambroise Fayolle, European Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Síkela and FCMB Chief Executive Officer, Yemisi Edun. The operation, according to a statement, is EIB Global’s first investment covering the dairy sector outside the European Union and is fully aligned with Nigeria’s development objectives in sustainable agriculture and inclusion as well as environmental and social standards. The EIB Global financing will address market gaps in the dairy sector, enabling the growth of EU businesses in Nigeria requiring an increase in milk supply. With Nigeria as one of the world’s largest exporters of cocoa, the investments provided by EIB Global through FCMB will strengthen the industrial processing capacities along the whole value chain, provide liquidity support to cocoa cooperatives and farmers and improve the traceability of products. Compliance with the EU Regulation on Deforestation will be ensured, fostering biodiversity conservation and reducing environmental externalities while supporting inclusive rural development in line with EU standards, the EIB Group’s Climate Roadmap and the European Green Deal. Alongside the credit line, EIB Global is providing technical assistance to support FCMB’s climate action strategy and the Nigerian agriculture sector’s capacity to manage environmental and social risks. Add us to your Preferred Sources EIB Group President Nadia Calviño said, “The EIB Group invests in agricultural value chains in Africa – main drivers of food security and economic growth. “These projects also open business opportunities for EU companies in Nigeria, building a true win-win partnership.” Similarly, the EIB Vice-President Ambroise Fayolle said, “With this financial partnership with First City Monument Bank, EIB Global concretely supports Nigerian agribusinesses to grow competitively while meeting international environmental and social standards. “Such investment is important for the country in terms of employment, health and the economy, with real impact on the local population. It is a concrete example of the EU Global Gateway initiative in which the EIB Group, as the EU bank, is a key actor and partner in Africa.” Nigeria spends $1.19bn on food imports in six months Covenant varsity, experts seek solutions to Nigeria’s food crisis Industrialisation, small businesses next focus after infrastructure – Oyebanji European Commissioner for International Partnerships Jozef Sikela also said, “Nigeria has enormous potential in agriculture. To turn that potential into more jobs, stronger businesses and new economic opportunities, we need to ensure that more value is created and retained in Nigeria. This Global Gateway investment with EIB Global and First City Monument Bank will help businesses across the cocoa and dairy value chains access the finance they need to grow and expand local processing. That is how we build stronger value chains and deepen the EU-Nigeria partnership for the benefit of both sides.” FCMB Chief Executive Officer Yemisi Edun said, “For farmers and agribusinesses, access to finance can make the difference between selling raw produce and building businesses that process more, earn more and create more jobs. “Through our partnership with EIB Global, businesses across Nigeria’s cocoa and dairy value chains will have access to the long-term funding needed to increase production, expand processing capacity and reach new markets. By combining financing with technical support, we aim to strengthen rural livelihoods, promote sustainable growth and help build a more resilient agricultural sector.” The project aligns with the EU’s geopolitical priorities and Nigeria’s development plans by supporting sustainable food systems and strategic food autonomy. The investment also contributes to the Team Europe Initiative on Green Economy, which promotes climate-smart agriculture, inclusive agribusiness, rural access and access to agricultural markets. Overall, in Nigeria, the EIB Group has invested €2.3bn since the start of its activities in the country in 1978. The financing has supported impactful and transformative investments in crucial areas for Nigeria such as sustainable urban transport, climate adaptation, innovation and digitalisation, and agribusiness logistics as well as small and medium enterprises and mid-caps. The European Investment Bank is the long-term lending institution of the European Union, owned by its Member States, financing investments that contribute to EU policy objectives. EIB Global is the EIB Group’s specialised arm devoted to increasing the impact of international partnerships and development finance, and a key partner of Global Gateway, aiming to support €100bn of investment by the end of 2027. FCMB provides personal, business, and corporate banking services across Nigeria, empowering individuals and businesses to pursue their goals while fostering inclusive and sustainable growth in the communities it serves. Global Gateway is the EU’s positive offer to reduce the worldwide investment disparity and boost smart, clean, and secure connections in digital, energy and transport sectors, and to strengthen health, education, and research systems, aiming to mobilise up to €300bn in public and private investments from 2021 to 2027.
